notes: Genuine New Arrivals PLP found in the main header navigation: the 'New Arrivals' primary nav item (data-title="New Arrivals") links directly to https://www.chumbak.com/collections/new-arrival; the same URL also appears a second time inside the 'Collections' mega-menu's own link list and in the mobile sidebar nav, confirming it is the single canonical listing (no alias/duplicate URL found -- checked the 554-collection list via /collections.json for any other new-arrival/new-in/just-in/latest-drop-named handle; only 'new-arrival' itself and a throwaway promo collection 'flat-15-off-on-new-arrivals' (a percent-off campaign collection, not a genuine new-arrivals listing, not linked anywhere in nav/footer/sitemap, excluded) were found). Opened the page and confirmed it is a real PLP, not editorial: page title/H1 is 'LATEST DROP' (a retail-new-arrivals framing), it has standard collection toolbar controls (sort including 'Date, new to old', grid/list layout switch, filters) and a real product grid. Exact qty verified two ways: (1) the theme's own rendered toolbar text 'collection-toolbar__products-count' = '403 products' on the live page; (2) independently enumerated by paging https://www.chumbak.com/collections/new-arrival/products.json?limit=250 to exhaustion and de-duplicating product IDs per the prior pass's Rule 1 method (never trust the /collections.json products_count metafield, which is confirmed inflated elsewhere on this store) = 403 unique product IDs, page 2 returned 153 products confirming pagination ended correctly. Both methods agree exactly. Checked the 'Collections' mega-menu's separate 'New Collections' sub-heading (Forest Folklore, Citrus Zest, Rare & Wild, Lost in Paradise, Palace Memoirs, Kashmir Trails, Summer Serenade, Digital Nomad, Marigold) and the Watches mega-menu's identical 'New Collections' list -- these are permanent named print/design product lines (a recurring Chumbak merchandising pattern per the prior Home-Decor pass notes), not date-based 'recently added' listings, and each sits alongside its own separate, already-identified 'New Arrivals' link in the same menu, so they were excluded as a distinct concept rather than treated as New Arrivals sub-categories. No other genuine site-defined New Arrivals children (e.g. per-category new-arrivals) were found in nav, footer, or the /pages/site-map SEO sitemap page -- this is a single, undifferentiated listing.
